source_records.page: Beeson (1941), original first edition, printed p.347, P. uncacanthurus line (primary image checked)
source_records.notes: ORIGINAL p.347 photograph directly verified 2026-10-27: this is primary-verifiable 1941 historical name use Platypus uncacanthurus, body length 6 mm and 'in Quercus lamellosa' association. Name is presented without an explicit sp. nov., taxon-distinguishing description, reference to another differentiating description, or proposed replacement on this page. For names first proposed after 1930, ICZN Article 13.1 requires diagnosis/definition, reference to such, or nomen novum; mere host and size list does not establish this. Check other passages/earlier descriptions before judging nomenclatural availability; possible nomen nudum pending, NOT established. This record's 'Source verified' qualifies the transcription/name usage only, NOT species-group availability or taxonomic synonymy. Separate host claim PLT_SR_000275; Park 2018:14–15 listed under lewisi but earliest synonymizing act unknown. Do not merge with P. lewisi.

source_records.page: Beeson, 1941. The Ecology and Control of the Forest Insects of India and the Neighbouring Countries, first edition, printed p.347, under PLATYPOD COL.
source_records.notes: Primary original-page image provided by curator and directly read 2026-10-27. Association evidence: historical author reports P. uncacanthurus 'in Quercus lamellosa' (plant name verified as accepted Quercus lamellosa Sm. in Kew POWO 2026, https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:296351-1). No explicit tree attack, rearing, emergence, galleries, experimental study, specimens or country for THIS line. Evidence type = host/wood association as published, uncertainty of method and locality retained. Beetle nomenclatural availability of 1941 name unresolved (ICZN Art 13.1) and synonymization with Platypus lewisi Blandford, 1894 NRE_000046 still Pending, so DO NOT adopt this host as verified for P. lewisi and DO NOT change China Distribution Summary. Original name usage evidence PLT_SR_000271 separately verified. SRL relation denotes provisional taxonomic concept linkage only, not adopted synonymy.

source_records.page: Browne (1980), Kontyû 48(4):497–498, P. lunatulus sp. nov.; type labels p.498
source_records.notes: B05 original primary verified 2026-10-26/27 from user-supplied scans pp.497–498, Browne 1980 IV. Original spelling Platypus lunatulus, explicit sp. nov., male and female diagnostic descriptions; male holotype and 1 male + 1 female paratypes. Holotype from Keelung (Formosa)→Nagoya on Quercus sp. timber, 8.V.1980, N. Shimizu. This supersedes earlier cross-source-only rating. Distinct PLT_SR_000274 records Quercus sp. wood association. Mandokwari/New Guinea type line atop p.497 belongs prior species, DO NOT assign to P. lunatulus. Type label is wood interception, not proof of wild Taiwan population or tree attacked in situ. Conflicting P. tayabasi taxonomic synonymy not settled.

source_records.page: Browne (1980), Kontyû 48(4):498, holotype/paratype label

source_records.page: Murayama 1931, Supplementary notes on the Platypodidae of Formosa III, printed p.198; original description begins p.197
source_records.notes: ORIGINAL published attacked-tree record primary verified p.198 in user-supplied scan. Beetle as originally named P. Niijimai Murayama n.sp.; two collected specimens, exact 'Trees attacked.—Psidium guajacum LINN.' Host original spelling preserved. Potential mapping to Psidium guajava L. is plausible and suggested in Beaver & Liu 2013, and P. guajava is an accepted plant in POWO (https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/600841-1), BUT the original guajacum name is not independently botanically validated as an exact synonym, so normalized host ID/Current Host Summary held Pending nomenclatural interpretation. This is credible DIRECT species-tree-attacked evidence, not an unconfirmed beetle occurrence. Taiwan specimen locality is explicit; do not infer broader geographic range.
